skill.name: internal-comms
skill.description: Helps draft internal company communications using structured formats for 3P updates, newsletters, FAQs, status reports, leadership updates, and project updates.
skill.summary: Drafts concise internal communications using company-style templates for updates, newsletters, FAQs, and status reports.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: All six static findings are false positives caused by prose and Markdown formatting. I found no prompt injection, command execution, credential access, or data exfiltration intent in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Markdown backtick file paths triggered command-execution alerts.
remediation.suggestion: Use Markdown links or plain filenames for guideline references to reduce future scanner noise.

remediation.issue: The skill asks assistants to gather internal context from company tools when available.
remediation.suggestion: Add a privacy note telling users to use only authorized sources and avoid unnecessary confidential details.

content.value_statement: Internal updates are hard to keep consistent across teams. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to draft concise updates in company formats.
actual_capabilities: Drafts 3P updates with Progress, Plans, and Problems sections.
Creates company newsletters with short bullets and clear sections.
Writes employee FAQ answers with source links and uncertainty notes.
Adapts general internal messages after clarifying audience, purpose, tone, and format.
Suggests useful internal sources such as Slack, email, calendar, and documents.
limitations: Does not access Slack, email, calendar, or documents without available tools.
Cannot verify facts unless the user provides sources or tool access.
Does not include a dedicated incident report template.
May need extra company style guidance for brand-specific wording.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Company Newsletter
use_cases.description: Turn leadership announcements, product milestones, and major updates into a short company-wide newsletter.

use_cases.title: Write a Weekly 3P Update
use_cases.description: Convert team progress, next plans, and blockers into a concise update for leadership.

use_cases.title: Answer Common Employee Questions
use_cases.description: Summarize frequent employee questions and draft clear answers based on official communications.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Simple Team Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a 3P update for the support team. Use these notes: progress, resolved backlog; plans, improve handoff process; problems, weekend coverage gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Newsletter From Notes
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with multiple company updates.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a company newsletter from these announcements. Group related items, keep bullets short, and use a professional internal tone.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Employee FAQ
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for questions and answers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write FAQ answers for employees about this policy change. Use only the attached source notes and flag any answer that needs executive approval.

prompt_templates.title: Synthesize Cross-Tool Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request using available internal sources.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use available Slack, email, calendar, and document context to draft a weekly leadership update. Include links only when they support company-wide decisions.

output_examples.input: Draft a 3P update for the product team using notes about launch progress, next sprint planning, and a design dependency.
output_examples.output: A concise 3P update with three labeled sections: Progress, Plans, and Problems. Each section uses one to three direct sentences.

output_examples.input: Create a company newsletter from several leadership announcements and product milestones.
output_examples.output: A grouped newsletter with short bullets for announcements, priority progress, leadership updates, and employee-facing news.

output_examples.input: Write FAQ answers for employees about a new office policy.
output_examples.output: A list of common questions with brief answers, source references, and notes where official confirmation is needed.

best_practices: Provide source notes, links, and the intended audience before asking for a draft.
Ask the assistant to flag uncertain facts instead of filling gaps.
Review sensitive internal details before sending any generated message.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a final announcement without giving source material.
Do not mix confidential team details into broad company updates.
Do not publish generated answers when executive approval is required.

faq.question: What kinds of communications can this skill draft?
faq.answer: It supports 3P updates, company newsletters, FAQ responses, status reports, leadership updates, project updates, and general internal messages.

faq.question: Does it connect to company tools by itself?
faq.answer: No. It can use Slack, email, calendar, or documents only when the assistant already has authorized access.

faq.question: Can it verify whether an update is accurate?
faq.answer: It can compare against provided sources, but final factual review remains the user responsibility.

faq.question: Is this skill useful for executives?
faq.answer: Yes. It can prepare concise leadership updates, but it still needs source notes and final review.

faq.question: Can it write company-wide newsletters?
faq.answer: Yes. It groups important announcements into short sections designed for Slack and email.

faq.question: How should sensitive information be handled?
faq.answer: Share only authorized source material and remove confidential details that are not needed for the audience.
